paper_title: SepLLM Accelerate Large Language Models by Compressing One Segment into   One Separator
caption: : Loss steps
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for several variants of a language model, including a baseline "Vanilla" model and multiple configurations of the SepLLM model with different segment sizes and hyperparameters. The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000, with a linear scale and tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents the loss, ranging from 2.4 to 3.4, also on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.1. Five distinct lines are shown: a purple line for "Vanilla", a blue line for "StrmLLM (n=64)", an orange line for "SepLLM (n=64)", a green line for "SepLLM (n=64, H)", and a red line for "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)", along with a dark blue line for "SepLLM (n=128)". All lines start at a loss value near 3.4 at iteration 0 and exhibit a steep decline in the initial phase, followed by a gradual flattening as training progresses. The "Vanilla" model (purple) achieves the lowest loss, stabilizing around 2.5 by 140,000 iterations. The "StrmLLM (n=64)" (blue) shows a higher final loss, stabilizing near 2.65. The "SepLLM (n=64)" (orange) and "SepLLM (n=64, H)" (green) lines are nearly identical, both converging to a loss of approximately 2.55. The "SepLLM (n=64, H/T)" (red) line is slightly above the orange and green lines, stabilizing around 2.57. The "SepLLM (n=128)" (dark blue) line is the highest among the SepLLM variants, stabilizing near 2.6. All lines show minor fluctuations (noise) during training, particularly evident in the blue and dark blue lines.
